checks.claim: The real orchestrator service becomes healthy before connector proof begins.
A provider-neutral connector connection can be registered without credential material.
A registered connector can be explicitly enabled for internal event ingestion.
A verified trusted low-risk message is normalized and routed to the executive agent as trusted.
Inbound source identity is derived from the registered provider/account rather than caller-supplied free text.
An unverified provider delivery cannot retain trusted-low-risk execution state.
Replaying the same provider event returns the original receipt and executive run rather than executing twice.
A connector-originated billing signal remains paused behind explicit owner approval.
The billing approval created from connector ingestion is visible on the normal pending-approval surface.
Duplicate provider delivery does not create a second persisted receipt.
Unique connector ingestion receipts are persisted for traceability.
The Phase 1 registry surface contains no passwords, OAuth tokens, API secrets or credential payloads.
Phase 1 preserves the no-external-send boundary and exposes no SEND_MESSAGES capability.
Unique connector events route into persisted executive-agent runs.
Evidence remains scoped to hosted synthetic provider deliveries and does not claim live provider authentication or external execution.
